# KBD Constraint Configuration — IPFS Sync for Obsidian

Project-specific rules derived from the stack (TypeScript Obsidian plugin, esbuild,
Node 24 CLI) and `DESIGN.md`. KBD and all executing tools read this file
during verification.

---

## Blocking Constraints (prevent archiving until resolved)

Universal + stack-specific:

```yaml
constraints:
  - id: no-console-log-in-commits
    severity: blocking
    description: 'No console.log statements in committed TypeScript/JavaScript'
    check: "grep -r 'console\\.log' src/ cli/ --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.js' --include='*.mjs'"

  - id: no-any-type
    severity: blocking
    description: 'No `any` type usage in TypeScript source (tsconfig strict is on)'
    check: "grep -rn ': any\\|as any\\|<any>' src/ cli/ --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx'"

  - id: no-hardcoded-secrets
    severity: blocking
    description: 'No hardcoded API keys, tokens, or passwords in source'
    check: "grep -rn 'sk-\\|api_key\\|API_KEY\\|secret.*=.*[\"\\x27][A-Za-z0-9]' src/ cli/"

  - id: build-passes
    severity: blocking
    description: 'Plugin bundle must build without errors'
    command: 'pnpm build'

  - id: webview-safe-bundle
    severity: blocking
    description: 'Plugin must run in Obsidian mobile WebView — no Node built-ins, no child_process, no native modules in src/'
    check: "grep -rn \"require('child_process')\\|require('fs')\\|require('path')\\|from 'node:\\|from 'fs'\\|from 'child_process'\" src/"

  - id: no-python
    severity: blocking
    description: 'No Python in this project: no *.py files, no python invocations in scripts, hooks or package scripts (spec 004)'
    check: "git ls-files '*.py' | grep . ; grep -rIn 'python' package.json cli/ tools/ .github/ 2>/dev/null"

  - id: kubo-args-in-query-string
    severity: blocking
    description: 'All kubo RPC args must travel in the query string (the prometheusags proxy drops form-encoded args)'
    note: 'Review every fetch/curl against the node; see README §node-quirks'

  - id: no-default-node
    severity: blocking
    description: "No built-in default IPFS RPC or gateway URL; the maintainer's open node must not be a default"
    check: "grep -rnE 'DEFAULT_RPC_URL|DEFAULT_GATEWAY_URL|prometheusags' src/ cli/ --exclude=retired-default-hosts.ts"
    note: 'Prints matches when violated; no output means it holds. The retired host string may appear only in src/core/config/retired-default-hosts.ts, where it is used to warn about a saved 0.2.0 URL and never to fill one in. tests/unit/no-default-node.test.ts enforces the same rule. Added with task 46.'
```

---

## Warning Constraints (acknowledge before archiving)

```yaml
- id: tests-for-new-features
  severity: warning
  description: 'Tests exist for all new features added in this change'
  note: 'No test runner wired yet; add one before Phase 1.1 implementation'

- id: no-stub-comments
  severity: warning
  description: 'No TODO/FIXME/STUB/HACK comments in committed code'
  check: "grep -rn 'TODO\\|FIXME\\|STUB\\|HACK' src/"

- id: design-doc-sync
  severity: warning
  description: 'DESIGN.md reflects the implemented behavior (schema changes, MFS layout, conflict policy)'
  note: 'Manual review required at archive time'

- id: never-sync-workspace-state
  severity: warning
  description: 'The exclusion definition (src/sync/exclusions.ts) keeps .trash/, workspace.json churn, and this dev folder out of sync payloads'
  check: "test \"$(grep -ohE '\"\\.trash/\"|\"\\.ipfs-sync/\"|\"\\.obsidian/\"' src/sync/exclusions.ts | sort -u | wc -l | tr -d ' ')\" = 3"
  note: 'Moved from scripts/excludes.txt in mvp-02 (task 2.2); passes whether or not scripts/excludes.txt exists. Updated 2026-10-03 (operator decision): mvp-07a task 1.3 replaced the individual .obsidian/workspace*.json, graph.json, cache and plugins/ entries with one ".obsidian/" entry that excludes the whole configuration folder (stricter, workspace state still never syncs), so the check now looks for that literal instead of ".obsidian/workspace.json"'
```

---

## Workflow Triggers

These run after each change iteration:

```yaml
workflow_triggers:
  - event: on_iteration_complete
    action:
      type: command
      target: 'pnpm build'

  - event: on_refinement_complete
    action:
      type: command
      target: "git add -A && git commit -m 'kbd: refine <change-id>'"
```

---

    severity: blocking
    description: 'No key/rm, pin/rm, or files/rm outside /obsidian-vault-sync/* on the shared node'
    note: 'All node mutations must target paths/keys created by this project'

+

+## Context
+
+The repo has no `.github/` at all (assessment, 2026-10-12). The donor at `~/Projects/prometheus/prometheus-skill-pack` ships a deployment-only `docs-pages.yml` with pinned action SHAs, a `paths: site/**` trigger, a concurrency group, and a policy comment that tests do not run in CI (local gates only) — allowed under the skill-pack's local-only rule, and this repo's AGENTS.md does not forbid it. The publication receipts for v0.2.0/v0.3.0/v0.4.0 are pending because the first-party-page condition has never been satisfiable; a deployed first-party docs site could satisfy it — evaluation only, no fabricated receipts.
+
+## Recorded decision: the About link cannot be set by the GitHub Action
+
+**Decision (recorded 2026-10-12):** the repository About link is set by a **one-time operator-authorized `gh repo edit --homepage https://prometheus-ags.github.io/obsidian-ipfs-sync/`**, run after the first green deploy. The user's literal ask — "the github action sets up the About link" — is **not achievable as stated** and this decision says so in the open.
+
+**Mechanism of the constraint:** GitHub Actions' `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot edit repository metadata. The Update-a-repository REST endpoint (`PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}`, which owns the `homepage` field) requires Administration write permission, which the workflow token does not carry and cannot be granted through `permissions:` in the workflow file.
+
+**Routes considered:**
+
+1. **One-time operator-authorized `gh repo edit --homepage <pages-url>` (recommended, chosen).** Simplest; the value is set once and never changes; no secret is created; the authorization is explicit and recorded in the task evidence. Verification is a readback: `gh api repos/Prometheus-AGS/obsidian-ipfs-sync --jq .homepage`.
+2. **PAT-secret-backed workflow step (fallback, rejected unless the operator rejects route 1).** A personal access token stored as a repo secret could call the endpoint from CI. Rejected as the default because it adds ongoing secret maintenance (rotation, expiry, scope review) to automate a set-once value — permanent cost for a one-time action. If the operator insists on in-workflow automation, task 4.3 changes shape and gains a secret-management prerequisite (phase plan, "Scope cuts and trade-offs").
+
+**Authorization boundary:** task 4.3 executes the chosen route only after operator authorization. If the operator declines all routes, the task records the refusal as its outcome; it does not fabricate a set link.
+
+## Decisions
+
+1. **Deployment-only workflow.** `docs-pages.yml` builds and deploys; it runs no tests. Rationale: the donor's own policy (tests are local gates), and the docs-02/docs-03 gates (sanitizer, `onBrokenLinks: throw`, `verify.mjs`, production build) already ran locally before merge. Adding a redundant CI test tier would double build time for no new signal.
+2. **Pinned SHAs.** Every action is pinned by full commit SHA, copied from the donor: checkout v4 `34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5`, configure-pages v5 `983d7736d9b0ae728b81ab479565c72886d7745b`, setup-node v4 `49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020`, upload-pages-artifact v3 `56afc609e74202658d3ffba0e8f6dda462b719fa`, deploy-pages v4 `d6db90164ac5ed86f2b6aed7e0febac5b3c0c03e`. Tag pins are mutable; SHAs are not. The donor's pins are the verified set (operator's production workflow).
+3. **Trigger and concurrency.** `paths: site/**` so docs-01-style README-only changes never trigger a deploy; concurrency group `pages-deploy` so a push during an in-flight deploy cancels or queues deterministically rather than racing the Pages artifact.
+4. **Node 24, npm ci.** The workflow uses node 24 with `npm ci` against the site's own lockfile — the npm/pnpm separation from docs-02 holds in CI exactly as locally.

A green workflow run proves the runner succeeded; only the fetch proves a reader can load the site (prior-context lesson: external integrations require at least one real-service test).
+6. **Receipt evaluation is recorded, not manufactured.** Task 4.4 evaluates the first-party-page condition per pending release and writes the verdict with reasoning. A "partial" or "no" is a valid outcome; an unverified "yes" is not.

+## Risks / Trade-offs
+
+- [The literal ask is not honored] -> surfaced, not silently substituted: proposal, design and task 4.3 all state the `GITHUB_TOKEN` constraint; the operator chooses the route.
+- [Pages enablement is a repo-settings mutation outside git] -> executed only with operator authorization; evidence records the API calls made.
+- [Pinned SHAs age] -> accepted: the donor maintains the same pins; a deliberate alignment pass updates both sites together.
+- [First deploy may fail on Pages enablement ordering] -> task 4.2 enables Pages before triggering the deploy; a failed first run is diagnosed, not retried blindly.
+
+## Migration Plan
+
+Nothing exists to migrate — no prior workflow, no prior Pages config. Rollback: `git revert` removes the workflow; Pages can be disabled in repo settings; the homepage field can be cleared with `gh repo edit --homepage ""`. All reversible.

+- **Custom domain** later: the `SITE_URL`/`BASE_URL` env pattern (docs-02) accommodates one without workflow changes; out of scope here.

+---
+title: CLI reference
+description: Every ipfs-sync command, its flags, the environment variables, config precedence and exit codes — checked against cli/help-text.ts and cli/args.ts.
+---
+
+# CLI reference
+
+<!-- source: cli/help-text.ts; cli/args.ts; README.md L444-548 -->
+
+The CLI is a plain Node HTTP client against the kubo RPC and gateway — no local
+IPFS daemon. Requires Node >= 24.15. Build with `pnpm install && pnpm build`,
+then run `node dist/cli/ipfs-sync.mjs ...` or the `ipfs-sync` bin. Everything
+below is also in `ipfs-sync --help`.
+
+## Commands
+
+```bash
+ipfs-sync status
+ipfs-sync init <vault> [--passphrase-file <path>]
+ipfs-sync publish <vault> [--repair] [--recover-slots] [--break-lock]
+    [--allow-full-reupload] [--allow-mass-removal]
+ipfs-sync pull <vault> [--name <ipns-id>] [--root-cid <cid> | --manifest <cid>]
+    [--allow-rollback | --resolve-fork] [--expect-min-sequence <n>] [--expect-vault-id <id>]
+    [--accept-first-pull] [--accept-replace] [--max-bytes <n>] [--accept-large]
+ipfs-sync pull <vault> --list-versions
+ipfs-sync keys change-passphrase <vault> [--cost standard|high] [--passphrase-file <path>]
+    [--accept-no-revocation] [--allow-downgrade]
+ipfs-sync keys increase-cost <vault> --cost standard|high [--accept-no-revocation]
+ipfs-sync keys accept-slots <vault> [--name <id> | --root-cid <cid> [--allow-rollback]] [--allow-downgrade]
+ipfs-sync keys discard <vault> [--yes-discard]
+ipfs-sync prune-history <vault> --keep <n> [--dry-run | --yes-prune]
+ipfs-sync abandon <vault> [--yes-abandon]
+ipfs-sync history [--limit <n>]
+```
+
+<!-- source: cli/help-text.ts L24-144 -->
+
+- **status** — node identity, MFS listing, gateway fetch, write probe and key
+  state.
+- **init** — the only command that creates an encrypted vault: generates the
+  passphrase (25 characters, five groups of five; never one you choose) and the
+  key slots. See [desktop setup](setup-desktop.md#create-the-encrypted-vault-ipfs-sync-init).
+- **publish** — encrypt and send only changed files to the node's MFS, then
+  publish the snapshot to the IPNS key. Needs the vault passphrase and an MFS
+  root strictly below `/obsidian-vault-sync`; never creates a vault.
+- **pull** — fetch only files whose sha256 differs, from an encrypted root.
+  Authenticates the manifest, checks the sequence against this device's record,
+  writes only verified files, keeps local edits as dated conflict copies and
+  never applies remote deletions. A plaintext (release 0.2.0) root is refused.
+- **keys change-passphrase** — replace the key slot under a new generated
+  passphrase, wrapping the same vault key. Revokes nothing (see
+  [Security](security.md)).
+- **keys increase-cost** — rewrap under the same passphrase at a higher
+  Argon2id cost (`--cost standard|high` required).
+- **keys accept-slots** — adopt the node's current key-slot file after another
+  device rewrapped. Pulls no files and does not raise the sequence floor; run
+  `pull` afterwards.
+- **keys discard** — drop an unfinished key-management operation (rewrap or
+  prune) this device cannot finish.
+- **prune-history** — remove the oldest history files from the node's
+  `manifests/` so that `--keep <n>` remain (at least the newest 20 are kept
+  whatever `--keep` says), then republish the root under the same sequence.
+- **abandon** — move this device's local files for a root (key-slot copy,
+  state, publish journal, key-management journal) into an
+  `abandoned-<h>-<ms>/` backup folder. Never contacts the node and deletes
+  nothing; needs neither the RPC nor the gateway URL.
+- **history** — print this device's own sync operations from the per-user
+  on-disk log, newest first. Reads only, sends no request. Not to be confused
+  with `prune-history`, which mutates the node.
+
+## Global flags
+
+<!-- source: cli/help-text.ts L146-222 -->
+
+- `--config <path>` — config file (default `./ipfs-sync.config.json` if
+  present; endpoints and non-secret fields only).
+- `--rpc-url <url>`, `--rpc-port <port>` — RPC (write) endpoint. Required.
+- `--gateway-url <url>`, `--gateway-port <port>` — gateway (read) endpoint.
+  Required; it is never derived from the RPC URL.
+- `--mfs-root <path>` — default `/obsidian-vault-sync/default`; publish needs a
+  root strictly below `/obsidian-vault-sync`.
+- `--key <name>` — IPNS publication key name (default `obsidian-vault-sync`;
+  must match `^obsidian-vault(-[a-z0-9-]+)?$`).
+- `--owned-key <id>` — an IPNS key ID this installation owns (repeatable; for
+  this run only, never written to the config file).
+- `--auth <scheme>` (`none | basic | bearer | header`), `--auth-user <user>`,
+  `--auth-header-name <name>` — endpoint authentication.
+- `--passphrase-file <path>` — for `init` and `keys change-passphrase`: write
+  the generated passphrase to this new file (0600). There is no `--passphrase`
+  option.
+- `--show-request` — print each request (method, URL, headers) with credential
+  headers redacted.
+- `-h`, `--help`.
+
+Command-specific flags: `--repair`, `--recover-slots`, `--break-lock`,
+`--allow-full-reupload`, `--allow-mass-removal` (publish); `--name`,
+`--root-cid`, `--manifest`, `--allow-rollback`, `--resolve-fork`,
+`--expect-min-sequence`, `--expect-vault-id`, `--accept-first-pull`,
+`--accept-replace`, `--max-bytes`, `--accept-large`, `--list-versions` (pull);
+`--cost`, `--accept-no-revocation`, `--allow-downgrade` (keys); `--keep`,
+`--dry-run`, `--yes-prune` (prune-history); `--yes-discard` (keys discard);
+`--yes-abandon` (abandon); `--limit` (history).
+
+## Environment variables
+
+<!-- source: cli/help-text.ts L224-240 -->
+
+```bash
+IPFS_SYNC_RPC_URL, IPFS_SYNC_RPC_PORT, IPFS_SYNC_GATEWAY_URL, IPFS_SYNC_GATEWAY_PORT,
+IPFS_SYNC_MFS_ROOT, IPFS_SYNC_KEY
+IPFS_SYNC_AUTH_SCHEME, IPFS_SYNC_AUTH_USER, IPFS_SYNC_AUTH_PASSWORD,
+IPFS_SYNC_AUTH_TOKEN, IPFS_SYNC_AUTH_HEADER_NAME, IPFS_SYNC_AUTH_HEADER_VALUE
+IPFS_SYNC_RPC_AUTH_* / IPFS_SYNC_GATEWAY_AUTH_*   # per-endpoint overrides, same suffixes
+IPFS_SYNC_PASSPHRASE_FILE, IPFS_SYNC_PASSPHRASE   # the vault passphrase; set at most one
+IPFS_SYNC_DEVICE                                  # device name recorded in the manifest
+```
+
+**Config precedence: flag > environment > config file > defaults.**
+
+## Credentials never come from the command line
+
+<!-- source: cli/args.ts L177-206; README.md L497-507 -->
+
+`--auth-password`, `--auth-token` and `--auth-header-value` do not exist; they
+are refused by name with exit 2, because the process list and shell history
+would show the value. The refusal names the replacement environment variable
+(`IPFS_SYNC_AUTH_PASSWORD`, `IPFS_SYNC_AUTH_TOKEN`,
+`IPFS_SYNC_AUTH_HEADER_VALUE`; per endpoint, `IPFS_SYNC_RPC_AUTH_*` or
+`IPFS_SYNC_GATEWAY_AUTH_*`) and never echoes the value. The same rule covers
+the vault passphrase: no `--passphrase` flag exists.
+
+Two related rules: a `./ipfs-sync.config.json` found in the working directory
+is refused (exit 2) when it sets a node address while a credential is
+configured by environment or flags — pass `--config <path>` to use a file on
+purpose; and a plain `http:` endpoint with a credential on a non-loopback host
+gets a warning (anyone on the network path can read the credential).
+
+The global auth is the RPC credential. The gateway inherits it only when both
+endpoints share an origin (scheme, host, port); on any other origin the gateway
+gets no credential unless you set `IPFS_SYNC_GATEWAY_AUTH_*` explicitly.
+
+## The pull confirmation ceiling, and what the CLI does not have
+
+<!-- source: README.md L471-484 -->
+
+`pull` asks before fetching more than 512 MiB of file content
+(`--max-bytes <n>` changes the ceiling; `--accept-large` is the non-interactive
+yes). In the v0.4.0 demo the first pull of a ~954.9 MiB vault stopped at this
+ceiling with exit 1 and fetched nothing until re-run with `--accept-large` —
+see [Evidence](evidence.md).
+
+**The CLI has no read cap and no exclusion option.** Both exist only in the
+plugin (the per-file read cap setting and the user exclusion list). A CLI
+publish reads a file of any size and applies only the built-in exclusion list.
+This is documented as-is; it is not fixed here. In the demo, the vault's
+195.4 MiB file published uncapped.
+
+## Exit codes
+
+<!-- source: cli/help-text.ts L244-258; README.md L477-480 -->
+
+- **0** — ok (for `pull`, 0 also covers paths skipped as expected, such as
+  `.obsidian/` or excluded paths from an older manifest; for `history`, 0 also
+  means no operations recorded).
+- **1** — a check, publish or pull failed: a file failed verification or was
+  not fetched, a path was skipped as unsafe, or the run stopped at a check
+  (wrong passphrase, rollback, fork, a held lock, an unconfirmed question). A
+  confirmation that was asked and declined also exits 1.
+- **2** — usage, unsafe configuration or a refused destination; no request is
+  sent. A plaintext (release 0.2.0) root is one such refusal. A command that
+  needs a confirmation and has neither a terminal nor its confirming flag
+  (`--accept-no-revocation`, `--yes-prune`/`--dry-run`, `--yes-discard`,
+  `--yes-abandon`) exits 2 before any request; `pull --resolve-fork` has no
+  confirming flag, so without a terminal it always exits 2.
+
+A question is asked only when standard input, standard output and standard
+error are all terminals; with any of the three redirected, the run cannot ask.
+
+## Interrupted operations
+
+<!-- source: README.md L781-854; cli/help-text.ts L86-89, L136-137 -->
+
+A pending rewrap or prune is finished by running the same command again — the
+rerun needs none of the confirming flags and takes what to finish from the
+journal; the rest of that command line is ignored. `keys discard` drops the
+operation when a rerun cannot finish it. After a killed publish, the next
+`publish` resumes, adopts or discards the journal based on the node's
+authenticated manifest; `--repair`, `--recover-slots` and `--break-lock` exist
+for the refusal cases and are described in `--help` and in the operator runbook
+(`docs/operator/encrypted-vault.md` in the repository).

+---
+title: How it works
+description: The snapshot sync model — MFS staging on a kubo node, an IPNS mutable pointer, the encrypted layout, delta publish and the pull conflict policy.
+---
+
+# How it works
+
+<!-- source: README.md L45-77; DESIGN.md §8.3, §8.4, §8.10 -->
+
+IPFS Sync is a snapshot synchronizer. Each publish encrypts the vault's changed
+files, stages them in a working tree on your kubo node, and moves one mutable
+pointer to the new snapshot. Each pull resolves that pointer, authenticates the
+snapshot's manifest and fetches only the files whose content hash differs.
+
+## The node and the working tree
+
+<!-- source: README.md L47-62; DESIGN.md §8.3 (MFS layout row) -->
+
+The server side is a stock **kubo** node you run or trust. The tool talks to it
+over the kubo RPC API (writes) and the gateway (reads); there is no local IPFS
+daemon on your device. Every vault lives in an **MFS** (Mutable File System)
+root strictly below `/obsidian-vault-sync`, one root per vault. MFS is the
+staging area: blobs land there first, and only a verified snapshot is pinned
+and published.
+
+The root holds exactly four entries:
+
+- `current/` — the encrypted files, each under an opaque 52-character name
+  (an HMAC of its path) inside two-character prefix folders;
+- `manifests/` — one encrypted history copy of the manifest per publish, named
+  `<16-digit sequence>-<rootCID>.enc` (a development build wrote
+  `<rootCID>.enc`, which still reads);
+- `manifest.enc` — the encrypted manifest of the current snapshot;
+- `keyslots.json` — the public key-slot file (see [Security](security.md)).
+
+## The mutable pointer
+
+<!-- source: README.md L57-64 -->
+
+An **IPNS key** on your node (default name `obsidian-vault-sync`) is the only
+mutable part. Each publish points it at the CID of the MFS root; `publish`
+creates the key if absent and records its ID in the config file (`ownedKeys`).
+Readers resolve the name to the current snapshot CID. DNSLink can replace the
+name with a human-readable one on a domain you control — same content, one DNS
+record.
+
+## Delta publish
+
+<!-- source: README.md L738-779; DESIGN.md §8.4 -->
+
+A publish compares the vault against its own record on plaintext sha256 and
+size; a file whose size and modification time match the record is not read
+again. Only changed files are encrypted and uploaded — a changed file is
+re-encrypted and uploaded whole, and a rename is a delete plus a new upload,
+because the node name is bound into the encryption. The run then writes
+`manifest.enc` and its history copy, reads the snapshot back through its
+immutable `/ipfs/<cid>/` path, and only then pins it and publishes the IPNS
+record. Any failure before the IPNS record leaves the previous pointer
+unchanged; a run with no changes writes nothing. Every file a publish skips
+(for example one deleted or changed mid-read) is named with its reason, so the
+published set is exact.
+
+## Pull and the conflict policy
+
+<!-- source: README.md L66-77, L236-247 -->
+
+Pull never deletes and never loses data. Each file is compared on plaintext
+sha256 three ways: this device's file, the baseline of the last pull or
+publish, and the node's copy.
+
+- A file this device did not edit is replaced by the node's version.
+- A file only this device edited stays.
+- Where both changed (or there is no baseline), the node's version takes the
+  path and the local content is preserved as `name (ipfs conflict
+  YYYY-MM-DD).ext` — the extension is kept so the copy opens in the same app.
+- Remote deletions are reported, not applied: a file deleted on the publishing
+  side stays on the receiving side.
+
+A pull fetches each file from the immutable tree the authenticated manifest
+names — never the mutable `current/` — decrypts it into `.ipfs-sync/tmp/` and
+renames it into place only when its size and sha256 equal the manifest entry.
+The CLI and the plugin run the same pull engine. Pull also refuses manifest
+paths it must not write (absolute paths, `..` segments, anything inside
+`.ipfs-sync/` or `.obsidian/`, excluded paths, and names another platform can
+write that this one cannot take safely); a refused path is skipped and the rest
+of the pull continues. True merging arrives with the Phase 2 op-log — see the
+[roadmap](roadmap.md).
+
+## The publish/pull flow
+
+```mermaid
+flowchart LR
+    subgraph device[Your device]
+        vault[Vault files]
+        engine[Sync engine<br/>encrypt · diff · verify]
+        state[Local state<br/>.ipfs-sync/]
+        vault --> engine
+        engine <--> state
+    end
+    subgraph node[Your kubo node]
+        mfs[MFS working tree<br/>current/ · manifests/<br/>manifest.enc · keyslots.json]
+        ipns[IPNS key<br/>obsidian-vault-sync]
+        mfs --> ipns
+    end
+    engine -->|publish: encrypted blobs<br/>over the RPC API| mfs
+    mfs -->|read back, pin,<br/>name/publish| ipns
+    ipns -->|pull: resolve name| engine
+    mfs -->|pull: fetch by CID<br/>through the gateway| engine
+```
+
+## What a second device does
+
+<!-- source: README.md L290-292 -->
+
+A second device uses the same MFS root and publication key name, adopts the
+owned key (its ID in `ownedKeys`, or `--owned-key <id>` for one CLI run), and
+pulls before its first publish. Two devices take turns; they do not publish at
+the same time. Concurrent publishes are narrowed by a name re-check, not
+prevented — kubo has no compare-and-swap (see
+[Limitations](limitations.md)).

+---
+title: Limitations and troubleshooting
+description: The limits that stay, what is not verified, and what to do when the tool refuses — with a pointer to the operator runbook.
+---
+
+# Limitations and troubleshooting
+
+These lists exist because they are the cases where the tool's checks can give a
+false sense of safety. They are stated, not smoothed over.
+
+## Limits that stay
+
+<!-- source: README.md L928-944 -->
+
+- **Removing 49 percent of the entries is silent.** The mass-removal guard
+  stops a publish that would remove every remaining entry, or more than half of
+  at least two — and not the first publish of a vault. Half and below proceed
+  unasked. An unmounted vault folder looks like every file deleted and is
+  caught; a half-mounted folder missing less than half the entries is not. The
+  guard protects the publish, not the node: the node keeps every old root.
+- **Silent per-file corruption of unchanged files by someone who can write to
+  the node is not detected by the publisher.** The publisher does not re-read
+  blobs it did not write in this run; a reader that decrypts one will notice.
+- **Concurrent publishes are narrowed, not prevented.** kubo has no
+  compare-and-swap. A publish re-reads the name before its first write and
+  again before `name/publish` and refuses if it moved, but a write race on the
+  shared tree is not detected at all.
+- **The sequence floor does not stop a node from showing an old copy to a
+  device that has no recorded state.** A first pull, a reinstalled plugin and a
+  deleted per-user state directory all have no record, and a freeze (withheld
+  updates) is never detected. Someone who holds the vault key can also publish
+  a very high sequence that every device then records.
+- **Rewrap does not revoke the old passphrase or any old copy of the key
+  slot.** Only re-encrypting the vault under a new key would revoke, and
+  nothing here does that.
+- **A vault published by release 0.2.0 cannot be pulled by this version.** The
+  plaintext reader is gone; a plaintext root is refused ("plaintext
+  publications are no longer supported by this version", CLI exit 2). Use
+  release 0.2.0 for those roots, and treat everything it published as public.
+
+Further standing limits, with their mechanics:
+
+<!-- source: README.md L326-442, L856-885 -->
+
+- **History growth.** Every non-empty publish adds one encrypted history file
+  to `manifests/`, pinned forever. The tool warns at 1,500 files and refuses at
+  1,999, naming `ipfs-sync prune-history`; a folder above 2,000 entries cannot
+  be listed and cannot be pruned — the way out is a new MFS root. An
+  auto-publish timer at 15 minutes on a vault that changes every tick reaches
+  the warning in about 15.6 days and the refusal in about 20.8 days unless you
+  prune.
+- **The desktop transport has no request timeout** (accepted backlog): a node
+  that accepts the connection and then goes silent leaves the call pending.
+- **The plugin's publish lock is best effort**, not an atomic lock across
+  machines; a CLI publish and a plugin publish can overlap for up to one
+  heartbeat interval (about 60 s) on a platform where rename overwrites.
+- **A file whose size and modification time equal the recorded values is not
+  read again.** A restore that preserves both (`cp -p`, `rsync -t`) is missed
+  by the delta check until size or time changes.
+- **The plugin cannot detect symbolic links** (Obsidian's file adapter has no
+  `lstat`). The CLI refuses to write through a symlink; the plugin cannot make
+  that check. Do not place symlinks in a vault you sync.
+- **Large-file pull in the plugin is not advertised as working.** The plugin's
+  transport buffers whole responses; a gateway that ignores the Range header
+  makes large files `unfetched`.
+- **This is not a backup.** A published snapshot is only as safe as your
+  passphrase, the node and your own checks. Keep a separate backup.
+
+## Not verified
+
+<!-- source: README.md L962-986 -->
+
+Nothing in this list has been checked, and none of it should be assumed to
+work:
+
+- any part of the plugin's encryption flow inside Obsidian — pull, restore,
+  resolve fork, the key-management, mass-removal and cost dialogs, the measure
+  command — beyond the recorded v0.3.0 operator run on desktop;
+- the `keys` commands and `prune-history` against a real kubo node;
+- an encrypted publish or pull on a phone; a High-cost key slot on a phone;
+- Android, Windows and Linux;
+- large binary bodies and Range requests through `requestUrl`, and large-file
+  pull in the plugin;
+- rollback prevention beyond what a device already accepted;
+- an auth-protected kubo endpoint with the plugin;
+- HKDF, HMAC and AES-GCM under Obsidian's WebView.
+
+What was measured on an iPhone is on the [mobile setup](setup-mobile.md) page;
+it covers old plaintext builds only. The full verification status of the
+current release is on the [evidence](evidence.md) page.
+
+## Troubleshooting: refusals and what to do
+
+<!-- source: docs/operator/encrypted-vault.md L570-694 -->
+
+The tool refuses loudly instead of guessing. Every refusal below sends nothing
+to the node, or stops before anything is written. The authoritative mapping —
+every refusal message, its meaning and its action — is the operator runbook
+`docs/operator/encrypted-vault.md` in the repository ("Refusals and what to
+do"); if a message on your screen differs from any doc, the code wins and the
+doc is stale. The common cases:
+
+| The message says | What it means | What to do |
+|---|---|---|
+| `publishing needs the vault passphrase and none was supplied` | No file, no variable, no terminal | Set `IPFS_SYNC_PASSPHRASE_FILE`, or run on a terminal |
+| `both IPFS_SYNC_PASSPHRASE and IPFS_SYNC_PASSPHRASE_FILE are set` | Two passphrase sources | Unset one |
+| `the passphrase file is inside the vault folder` | The next publish would upload it | Keep the file outside the vault |
+| `unknown option --auth-password` (also `--auth-token`, `--auth-header-value`) | Credentials are never taken from the command line | Set the named `IPFS_SYNC_AUTH_*` environment variable |
+| `the state folder is a symbolic link` | `<vault>/.ipfs-sync` is a link | Replace it with a real folder |
+| `not a valid generated passphrase` | Wrong length or alphabet, or a probable typo | Copy the passphrase instead of retyping it |
+| `wrong passphrase or damaged key slot` | The commitment or wrap did not verify; one outcome by design | Retry with the right passphrase |
+| `this MFS root holds no encrypted vault yet` | Empty root, no local copy | Run `ipfs-sync init` |
+| `this MFS root holds a plaintext publication from an earlier release` | Release 0.2.0 output | Use a new `--mfs-root`; the old plaintext stays public |
+| `the node's key slots differ from this device's copy` | `keyslots.json` was replaced or damaged | Do not retry; check the node. If the vault is lost to you, a new root and a new vault |
+| `the node no longer holds this vault's key slots` | The file is gone from the node | New root, new vault; `abandon` moves the local files aside first |
+| `this device is not the publisher of the vault in this root` | Second device, or `.ipfs-sync/` was deleted | Run `pull` with the passphrase and the same MFS root |
+| `the node's manifest has sequence N, older than this device's record` | An older snapshot was put back | If this device's record is the truth: `publish --repair` |
+| `... sequence N ... this device's record has sequence M` (ahead) | Another device published | Run `pull` first, then publish again |
+| `the node holds a different manifest at sequence N` (fork) | Two devices published the same sequence | `pull --resolve-fork`, then publish |
+| `another publish is running in this vault` | `publish.lock` is held with a fresh heartbeat | Wait; if the holder is gone, `publish --break-lock` |
+| `this publish would remove N of M entries` | The mass-removal guard | Check the vault folder is mounted and complete; if intended, `--allow-mass-removal` |
+| `plaintext publications are no longer supported by this version` | A release 0.2.0 root | Nothing reads it; use a new MFS root |
+| `manifests/ ... already holds N history files ... stops at 1,999` | History limit | `ipfs-sync prune-history <vault> --keep <n>` |
+| `did not finish on this device, so publish and pull are paused` | A pending rewrap or prune journal | Run the same `keys`/`prune-history` command again; `keys discard` if it cannot finish |
+| `needs a terminal to confirm` | No terminal and no confirming flag | Run on a terminal, or pass the flag the message names |
+
+After a crash, a killed process or a dropped connection: run the same command
+again. Do not delete `.ipfs-sync/`. When a refusal ends in "use a new root and
+a new vault", `ipfs-sync abandon <vault>` (or the plugin's "Abandon this
+vault") moves this device's local files aside — read its preview first: a
+pending rewrap or prune is dropped, and its write to the node is not withdrawn.

+---
+title: Security
+description: The threat model as it stands — what is encrypted, what the node operator sees, public key slots and offline guessing, and the open-RPC warning.
+---
+
+# Security
+
+This page normalizes the threat model from `DESIGN.md` section 8 and the
+README's security section. The encryption is implemented; it has had static
+reads by models, and **no independent review by a human or an outside party is
+recorded**. Read the [limitations](limitations.md) page with this one.
+
+## What is encrypted, and what is not
+
+<!-- source: README.md L557-578; DESIGN.md §8.5 -->
+
+File contents, file paths and names, and the manifest are encrypted
+(AES-256-GCM) under a random 256-bit vault key. The vault key is stored on the
+node in `keyslots.json`, wrapped by a key derived from your passphrase with
+Argon2id (64 MiB, 3 iterations by default; a High preset of 128 MiB and 4
+iterations exists).
+
+What the node operator — or anyone who can write to the node — can still see:
+
+- the number of files and the **exact size of each file** (a blob's length is
+  its plaintext length plus a fixed overhead, so a file of known length is
+  recognisable);
+- when you publish and how often, and which encrypted blobs change;
+- that the vault exists, plus the IPNS and gateway access pattern.
+
+Such an operator can also delete, corrupt, replace or withhold any object, and
+can serve you an older valid snapshot. A pull refuses a sequence below the
+highest one this device recorded — which catches a replay only on a device that
+already accepted a newer one; a freeze (withheld updates) is not detected.
+
+Without the passphrase, and short of guessing it, the operator cannot read
+names, paths, contents or the manifest, cannot create content that
+authenticates under the vault key, and cannot make a publisher encrypt under a
+different key.
+
+## The key slot is public, forever
+
+<!-- source: README.md L568-578; DESIGN.md §8.5 -->
+
+Anyone who has a root CID can download `keyslots.json` and guess passphrases
+offline, at the cost of Argon2id, **with no deadline**. Every old root stays
+pinned on the node and this project never unpins one, so a leaked passphrase
+plus any old copy of the slot — including the copies inside earlier pinned
+roots — opens every state you ever published.
+
+That is why passphrases are generated, not chosen: 23 random symbols (115 bits)
+plus 2 check symbols from the RFC 4648 base32 alphabet. The check symbols are a
+typo guard, not a proof of randomness: they catch a mistyped body symbol with
+about 99.9% probability and a mistyped check symbol always, and about 1 in
+1,024 arbitrary 25-symbol strings passes by chance.
+
+**A passphrase change revokes nothing.** `keys change-passphrase` and
+`keys increase-cost` write a new slot around the same vault key; nothing is
+re-encrypted, and every old copy of the slot keeps opening the vault. Only
+re-encrypting under a new vault key would revoke access, and no code here does
+that.
+
+**There is no recovery.** Lose the passphrase and every copy of the key slots
+and the data is gone; nobody can reset it. The local copy of `keyslots.json`
+protects only against the node losing the file. Save the generated passphrase
+in a password manager before you publish.
+
+## The open-RPC warning
+
+<!-- source: README.md L1019-1038 -->
+
+The maintainer's own test node — the host that releases up to 0.2.0 built in as
+the default — accepted **unauthenticated writes from the entire internet** when
+last checked, and that is not closed. It is no longer a default precisely
+because a default would have sent every fresh install's encrypted blobs and
+their metadata to a node anyone can write to. It remains the maintainer's
+verification target only, and it hosts other projects' keys. **Never point a
+real vault at it.**
+
+If you configure a node that is open the same way, the same exposure applies to
+you: anyone can add or pin garbage, create IPNS keys, or republish your vault
+pointer if they learn its key name. Before a node becomes your sync backbone,
+put auth in front of the RPC (basic-auth or a bearer token at a proxy) or
+restrict `/api/v0` to your own IPs/VPN — and keep the RPC private long-term,
+exposing only a read-only gateway. With an encrypted vault on a hardened node,
+your notes are protected by the passphrase and by nothing else on the node: the
+node can still delete, replace or withhold objects, and see sizes and timing.
+
+## Plaintext local state
+
+<!-- source: README.md L887-905; DESIGN.md §8.5 -->
+
+Encryption protects what is on the node. Your notes sit in clear in the vault
+folder on every device. `<vault>/.ipfs-sync/` holds your file paths in
+plaintext, and its `tmp/` folder holds verified plaintext file content while a
+pull runs and after a crash. The plugin's `data.json` stores node and gateway
+credentials in plain text (it is never published; the whole `.obsidian/`
+folder is excluded). Keep `.ipfs-sync/` out of iCloud, Dropbox, Syncthing,
+backup tools and any repository. The sequence floor lives outside the vault —
+in a per-user directory for the CLI, in the plugin data for the plugin — so
+deleting the folder does not reset it.
+
+## Redirects
+
+<!-- source: README.md L371-399; DESIGN.md §8.7 -->
+
+A 301, 302, 303, 307 or 308 answer is refused on the shared request path with a
+fixed message; the `Location` is not shown and not followed. On **desktop**
+that refusal holds: requests go through Node's `http`/`https`, which return the
+3xx instead of following it, so a credential goes to the configured URL only.
+On **mobile it cannot hold**: Obsidian's `requestUrl` follows redirects itself,
+with no option to stop it and no way to read the final URL. **On iOS the plugin
+cannot stop a custom-header credential (for example `X-Api-Key`) from reaching
+another origin.** Use Bearer or Basic on a phone — iOS strips those on a
+cross-origin hop. The redirect guarantee exists only where Node's `http` is
+reachable; no setting adds it on mobile. Point the plugin only at an endpoint
+you control and trust not to redirect.
+
+## Passphrase handling in practice
+
+<!-- source: README.md L646-688 -->
+
+- `publish` and `pull` read the passphrase from exactly one of
+  `IPFS_SYNC_PASSPHRASE_FILE` (a 0600 file you own), `IPFS_SYNC_PASSPHRASE`, or
+  a non-echoing prompt. Setting both variables is an error; whatever you supply
+  is checked for the generated form before any request is sent.
+- An environment variable stays readable by your other processes, is inherited
+  by child processes, and can land in shell history and CI logs. Prefer the
+  prompt for interactive work and the 0600 file for automation.
+- The interactive `init` display leaves the passphrase in terminal scrollback
+  and in `script`/`tmux` logs.
+- The CLI overwrites the passphrase bytes it holds after key derivation on a
+  best-effort basis; strings cannot be overwritten, and the plugin's dialog
+  holds the passphrase in an interface string that cannot be zeroed.
+
+## What this does not provide
+
+<!-- source: DESIGN.md §8.5 non-goals -->
+
+Forward secrecy or revocation (the vault key never rotates); hiding file
+counts, sizes, timing or the vault's existence; detection of a freeze or of a
+stale first pull; protection for a device whose memory, environment or files
+are compromised; deletion of history (old roots stay pinned); recovery of a
+lost passphrase; device pairing and additional key slots (designed, not built —
+see the [roadmap](roadmap.md)); and hiding or encrypting the local state.

+---
+title: Desktop setup
+description: Install the Obsidian plugin from a GitHub release or from source, install the CLI, create an encrypted vault with init, and configure the settings tab.
+---
+
+# Desktop setup
+
+<!-- source: README.md L7-9 -->
+
+**There is no default node.** Nothing works until you enter the RPC URL and the
+gateway URL of a kubo node you run or trust, in the plugin's settings tab or
+the CLI's flags, environment or config file. With either one missing, every
+command refuses and sends no request.
+
+## Before anything else: harden the node
+
+<!-- source: README.md L1019-1038 -->
+
+The node is your sync backbone; treat its RPC endpoint as write access to your
+vault's pointer. The maintainer's own test node accepted **unauthenticated
+writes from the entire internet** when last checked; it is not a default and
+you should never point a real vault at it. Before you configure any node for
+real notes:
+
+- put auth in front of the RPC (for example basic-auth or a bearer token at a
+  reverse proxy), and configure the same credential in the plugin settings or
+  the CLI environment; or
+- restrict the RPC endpoint (`/api/v0`) to your own IPs or VPN.
+
+Long-term, keep the RPC private and expose only a read-only gateway for
+content. Details: [Security](security.md).
+
+## Install the plugin
+
+<!-- source: README.md L87-101; manifest.json -->
+
+Requires Obsidian 1.12.3 or later (`minAppVersion` in `manifest.json`).
+
+**From the GitHub release.** Download `main.js` and `manifest.json` from the
+release assets (v0.4.0 is a pre-release), copy both into
+`<vault>/.obsidian/plugins/ipfs-sync/`, then enable **IPFS Sync** under
+**Settings → Community Plugins**.
+
+**From source.** Requires Node >= 24.15 and pnpm:
+
+```bash
+pnpm install && pnpm build
+```
+
+`pnpm build` writes the plugin to `dist/plugin/` (`main.js` and
+`manifest.json`) and the CLI to `dist/cli/ipfs-sync.mjs`. Copy the two plugin
+files into `<vault>/.obsidian/plugins/ipfs-sync/` as above. For development,
+`pnpm dev` watches and rebuilds; with `OBSIDIAN_PLUGIN_DIR` set it writes
+straight into that plugin directory — note that this overwrites those files on
+every rebuild, so never point it at a vault you do not want overwritten.
+
+## Install and run the CLI
+
+<!-- source: README.md L444-489; cli/help-text.ts L4-22 -->
+
+The CLI is a plain Node HTTP client against the kubo RPC and gateway; it needs
+no local IPFS daemon. Build once, then run it directly or through the
+`ipfs-sync` bin:
+
+```bash
+node dist/cli/ipfs-sync.mjs status
+```
+
+`status` is a safe first command: it shows node identity, the MFS listing, a
+gateway fetch, a write probe and key state. Endpoints come from flags
+(`--rpc-url`, `--gateway-url`), the environment (`IPFS_SYNC_RPC_URL`,
+`IPFS_SYNC_GATEWAY_URL`) or the config file (`rpc.url`, `gateway.url`).
+Credentials come from the environment only — never the command line. The full
+surface is in the [CLI reference](cli-reference.md).
+
+## Create the encrypted vault: `ipfs-sync init`
+
+<!-- source: README.md L626-688; cli/help-text.ts L26-37 -->
+
+`init` is the only command that creates an encrypted vault; `publish` never
+creates one. It needs an MFS root strictly below `/obsidian-vault-sync` that is
+completely empty on the node:
+
+```bash
+node dist/cli/ipfs-sync.mjs init <vault> --mfs-root /obsidian-vault-sync/<name>
+```
+
+`init` generates the passphrase itself — 25 characters shown as five groups of
+five. You cannot choose your own. Two ways to receive it:
+
+- **Interactive** (default on a terminal): it prints the passphrase once and
+  asks you to type it again. What it printed stays in your terminal scrollback
+  and in `script`/`tmux` logs — clear or disable those first, or use the file
+  form.
+- **Automated**: `--passphrase-file <path>` writes the passphrase to a new
+  file (mode 0600, created exclusively) and prints only the path.
+
+Save the passphrase in a password manager before you publish. **A lost
+passphrase means the data is lost for good — there is no recovery.** Later
+`publish` and `pull` runs take the passphrase from `IPFS_SYNC_PASSPHRASE_FILE`,
+from `IPFS_SYNC_PASSPHRASE`, or from a prompt that does not echo. A passphrase
+file inside the vault is refused, because the next publish would upload it with
+the notes it protects.
+
+Then publish:
+
+```bash
+IPFS_SYNC_PASSPHRASE_FILE=<path> node dist/cli/ipfs-sync.mjs publish <vault> --mfs-root /obsidian-vault-sync/<name>
+```
+
+## The settings tab essentials
+
+<!-- source: README.md L105-234 -->
+
+Open **Settings → IPFS Sync**. Until both the RPC and gateway URLs are set the
+tab shows "Not configured", and publish, pull, status and the key actions
+refuse with "Set your IPFS node in settings" and send no request. The
+essentials:
+
+- **RPC and gateway endpoints** — URL plus optional port each. The gateway URL
+  is never derived from the RPC URL.
+- **Authentication** — none, basic, bearer or a custom header, per endpoint.
+  The gateway inherits the node credential only when both share an origin; an
+  explicit **Gateway authentication** choice always wins. Credentials are
+  stored in plain text in the plugin's `data.json`.
+- **Publication key name and MFS root** — the IPNS key and the staging root the
+  vault publishes under.
+- **Encryption section** — vault state (not set up, locked or unlocked), the
+  Lock/Unlock/Set up buttons, the pull record, key-derivation cost, and the
+  key-management and prune-history rows.
+- **Read cap** — the largest single file the plugin reads into memory (default
+  64 MB); a file above the cap is counted as failed and the rest continue.
+- **Ask before pulling more than (MB)** — the pull confirmation threshold
+  (default 512 MB).
+- **Auto-publish interval** (whole minutes, 0 = off) and **catch-up on load**
+  (one pull after startup; off by default).
+
+Commands (`Ctrl/Cmd+P`): **IPFS Sync: Publish vault**, **Pull vault**,
+**Restore an older version**, **Resolve fork**, **Show status** and **Measure
+key derivation time**. Two ribbon icons run Publish and Pull. The first Publish
+on a device with no vault opens the setup dialog, which shows the generated
+passphrase once and asks you to save it and type it again; the unlocked key is
+held in memory only, never in `data.json`.
+
+<!-- source: README.md L161-166 -->
+
+If you upgrade from a build that had a built-in node: that host is retired and
+open to anyone, so saved settings that name it are cleared at load and the
+credential tied to them is dropped. You must enter your node's URLs and
+credentials yourself.

+title: Mobile setup
+description: Installing the plugin on a phone through BRAT — a procedure for testers. Mobile sync is unverified; read the caveats before you touch a real vault.

+
+# Mobile setup
+
+:::danger Unverified on mobile
+**Mobile sync has never run** (standing verification gap T3). No encrypted
+publish or pull has run on a phone, and **Android is untested**. This page is a
+procedure for people testing the build, not a statement of support. Do not rely
+on it, and do not point it at a vault you cannot lose.
+:::
+
+<!-- source: README.md L40, L309-314, L441-442, L978-986 -->
+
+## The caveats, stated plainly
+
+<!-- source: README.md L309-314, L394-399, L616-618 -->
+
+- **Mobile sync has never run.** The encrypted flow — publish, pull, unlock,
+  every dialog — has not been exercised on a phone. Phone behaviour with a real
+  vault (memory under buffering, background and suspend) is unmeasured.
+- **Android is untested** and is not claimed at all.
+- On mobile, every request goes through Obsidian's **`requestUrl`, which buffers
+  each whole response body in memory and follows redirects**. The size caps and
+  streaming that protect the desktop path do not apply; there is no option to
+  stop a redirect and no way to read the final URL.
+- **Credential leak on redirect (iOS).** Because redirects are followed, a
+  custom-header credential (for example `X-Api-Key`) can leak cross-origin on
+  iOS — the header is forwarded to the redirect target. Use **Bearer or Basic**
+  on a phone: iOS strips those on a cross-origin hop. Point the plugin only at
+  an endpoint you control and trust not to redirect. See
+  [Security](security.md#redirects).
+- **No iCloud vaults, and no manual iCloud copies.** Do not install into an
+  iCloud vault or copy a vault through iCloud by hand: a manual copy hung the
+  app at "Loading plugins", a file-provider hang that cleared only by
+  restarting the phone.
+- **High-cost key slots may not unlock on a phone.** Whether a phone can
+  complete Argon2id at the High preset (128 MiB, 4 iterations) was not
+  measured. The default-cost derivation was timed on an iPhone (about 0.57–1.1
+  s depending on the build measured), but that says nothing about the encrypted
+  pull or a High-cost slot.
+
+What was actually measured on an iPhone (iOS 27.2 beta, Obsidian 1.13.7),
+recorded 2026-10-02 from operator screenshots and not reproduced by an agent:
+the release 0.2.0 **plaintext** pull of 5 files (24 KB) worked, as did pulls of
+a 50 MB and a 5 MB file, and Argon2id at the default cost completed in about a
+second. These are measurements of old plaintext builds. They say nothing about
+the current encrypted flow on a phone.
+
+<!-- source: README.md L99-101 -->
+
+The manifest sets `isDesktopOnly: false`, but that is a declaration, not
+evidence: mobile has not been run.
+
+## Installing through BRAT
+
+<!-- source: README.md L309-314 -->
+
+The exact plugin build reaches a phone through the BRAT plugin from a GitHub
+**pre-release that carries the reviewed bytes and has its own tag** — never the
+main release tag.
+
+1. On the phone, install and enable the
+   [BRAT](https://github.com/TfTHacker/obsidian42-brat) community plugin.
+2. In BRAT, add this repository (`Prometheus-AGS/obsidian-ipfs-sync`) and
+   select the pre-release tag that carries the build you intend to test (for
+   example `v0.4.0`). Do not track the main tag.
+3. Let BRAT install `main.js` and `manifest.json`, then enable **IPFS Sync**
+   under **Settings → Community Plugins**.
+4. Open the settings tab and enter the RPC URL and gateway URL of your own
+   hardened node — there is no default node on mobile either — with a Bearer or
+   Basic credential (never a custom header; see the caveats above).
+5. Use a throwaway vault. Not an iCloud vault, and not your notes.
+
+## If you test it anyway
+
+<!-- source: README.md L616-618, L978-986 -->
+
+- Expect the app to be slow or memory-pressured on large pulls: every response
+  body is buffered whole.
+- Unlock a default-cost vault by hand before expecting anything automated; the
+  auto-publish timer and catch-up pull never ask the passphrase or cost
+  questions.
+- A hang at "Loading plugins" after touching vault files through iCloud is the
+  known file-provider hang; restart the phone.
+- Report what you see. The honest status of this page is "unverified on
+  mobile", and a report is how that changes.

+#!/usr/bin/env node
+
+// Public-content sanitizer for the documentation site build.
+// Adapted from the prometheus-skill-pack donor's check-public-docs.mjs
+// forbidden-pattern approach, extended with this repo's rules.
+//
+// Scope: scan exactly what enters the site build — site/docs and site/src.
+// No docs plugin instance points outside site/, so repo docs/ is not part of
+// the build and is not scanned. If a plugin ever serves ../docs content, add
+// that root here in the same commit.
+
+import {readdir, readFile} from 'node:fs/promises';
+import os from 'node:os';
+import path from 'node:path';
+import {fileURLToPath} from 'node:url';
+
+const scriptDir = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
+const siteDir = path.resolve(scriptDir, '..');
+
+const roots = [path.join(siteDir, 'docs'), path.join(siteDir, 'src')];
+
+const scannable = /\.(md|mdx|js|jsx|ts|tsx|css)$/;
+
+const forbidden = [
+  {
+    label: 'machine-local home path',
+    pattern: new RegExp(
+      `${escapeRegExp(`${os.homedir()}${path.sep}`)}|/Users/[^/\\s]+/|/home/[^/\\s]+/`,
+      'g',
+    ),
+  },
+  {
+    label: 'literal bearer credential',
+    pattern: /Authorization:\s*Bearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9_-]{32,}/g,
+  },
+  {
+    label: 'literal 32-byte private key field',
+    pattern: /private[_-]?key\s*[:=]\s*["'][A-Za-z0-9+/_=-]{40,}["']/gi,
+  },
+  {
+    label: 'PEM private key block',
+    pattern: /BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY/g,
+  },
+  {
+    label: 'raw private wiki path',
+    pattern: /\.prometheus\/knowledge\/wiki\/[^\s)`]+/g,
+  },
+  {
+    label: 'device keyslot file reference',
+    pattern: /\bkeyslots\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.json/g,
+  },
+  {
+    label: 'device state file reference',
+    pattern: /\bstate\.[a-f0-9]{8,}\.json/gi,
+  },
+  {
+    label: 'node-access command (kubectl)',
+    pattern: /\bkubectl\b/g,
+  },
+  {
+    label: 'node-access context (know-me)',
+    pattern: /know-me/g,
+  },
+  {
+    label: 'node-access namespace (ipfs-0)',
+    pattern: /ipfs-0/g,
+  },
+];
+
+const findings = [];
+for (const root of roots) {
+  for (const file of await scannableFiles(root)) {
+    const content = await readFile(file, 'utf8');
+    const relative = path.relative(siteDir, file);
+    for (const rule of forbidden) {
+      rule.pattern.lastIndex = 0;
+      for (const match of content.matchAll(rule.pattern)) {
+        const line = content.slice(0, match.index).split('\n').length;
+        findings.push(`${relative}:${line}: ${rule.label}`);
+      }
+    }
+  }
+}
+
+if (findings.length > 0) {
+  console.error('Public documentation sanitizer rejected the following content:');
+  for (const finding of findings) console.error(`- ${finding}`);
+  process.exit(1);
+}
+
+console.log('Public documentation sanitizer passed.');
+
+async function scannableFiles(root) {
+  const entries = await readdir(root, {withFileTypes: true});
+  const files = [];
+  for (const entry of entries) {
+    const candidate = path.join(root, entry.name);
+    if (entry.isDirectory()) files.push(...(await scannableFiles(candidate)));
+    else if (entry.isFile() && scannable.test(entry.name)) files.push(candidate);
+  }
+  return files;
+}
